comments.body:
PROVEN RCA (rebar-debug Phase 1, 2026-08-09)

Mechanism: `summary_compute` resolves each requested identifier through `show_state`, but discards the resolved state's `alias` and returns the caller-supplied token as `ticket_id` (`src/rebar/_engine_support/gates.py:386-411`). The summary schema and CLI/library/MCP contracts likewise omit alias (`src/rebar/schemas/summary.schema.json:5-16`; `src/rebar/_lib_gates.py:205-212`; `src/rebar/_mcp_reads.py:260-263`). Thus a short prefix remains the most local identifier and is echoed back even after successful resolution: live `rebar summary b68c --output json` returned `ticket_id: b68c` with no alias, while `rebar show b68c` resolved the canonical ticket and exposed alias `anthracite-maize-frog`. The agent then copies the locally salient prefix.

Discriminating proof: pinned `bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0`, temperature 0, single-turn, 5 repeats x 5 tickets. Current guidance plus summaries whose local `ticket_id` values were four-character tokens yielded 25/25 four-character `rebar show` commands and 0/25 aliases, despite an earlier catalog containing every alias. Changing only the local summary to add each alias yielded 25/25 alias commands. Leaving summary unchanged but adding an adjacent affirmative alias rule also yielded 25/25 aliases. Removing only the AGENTS quick-reference `tid["id"]` example had no effect (0/25 aliases, 25/25 full IDs), rejecting example priming as the cause. With alias plus affirmative rule, the identity-sensitive negative control emitted full canonical UUIDs in 25/25 `rebar-ticket:` trailers, proving the intervention does not indiscriminately replace canonical identities.

Resolver alternative rejected: `_ids.py:278-310` resolves aliases and fails closed for ambiguous prefixes. Live 2dce/2e89 summary inputs were rejected as ambiguous, while aliases resolve. Resolver ergonomics is not the defect. `_short_prefix` already computes the shortest currently unique prefix (`src/rebar/_engine_support/lookups.py:46-61`).

Defect legitimacy: incomplete implementation of the approved WS5 agent-fitness intent. Original authority `c5d79b58b6e829b336684c46cfc482c17c111c7a:REMEDIATION_PROPOSAL.md`, WS5e lines 336-344, explicitly requires create to return id+alias so agents need no second show and requires interface parity; current library/MCP comments preserve that rationale (`_lib_writes.py:95-97`, `_mcp_writes.py:57-68`). The compact summary surface drops the agent-facing alias that WS5e made available.

Caller-dependency gate: expected post-fix behavior is additive alias availability/foregrounding on summaries while retaining fail-closed prefix resolution and canonical IDs for identity-sensitive contracts. Serena plus rg found only `summary_cli` and public `rebar.summary` as direct callers; MCP delegates to the library. The schema permits additive properties, contract tests validate shape rather than exact equality, and no caller was found that behaviorally depends on alias absence. No blocker to Phase 2.

Phase 1 stops here; no code/test change, claim, plan review, or ticket transition was performed.

comments.body:
Final rebar-debug report (ticket intentionally left in_progress; closure deferred)

Problem: agents copied collision-prone four-character prefixes instead of durable human-friendly aliases.

Proven root cause: summary_compute resolved ticket state but omitted state.alias while echoing the caller token; schema/library/MCP/CLI contracts institutionalized that alias-free shape. The adjacent agent guidance also did not affirm which identifier to retain.

Proof: pinned Haiku 4.5, temperature 0, 5 samples x 5 commands. Prefix-only local summaries produced 25/25 four-character commands. Adding the alias locally independently produced 25/25 aliases; adjacent affirmative guidance independently produced 25/25 aliases. Removing old examples did not change selection. The canonical-trailer control remained 25/25 full UUIDs.

Test: tests/unit/test_summary_alias_b68c.py was observed RED before repair (resolved KeyError alias; ambiguous output missing alias:null), held out from the fixer, then GREEN 2/2. Removing the two alias fields returned it to RED 2/2; restoration returned GREEN. The oracle uses library plus real CLI JSON and asserts observable outputs. Interface/schema suite passed 24/24.

Fix: compact summaries now carry exact resolved alias and unknown/ambiguous results carry alias:null while ticket_id preserves the caller token. Schema plus library/MCP/CLI/generated references were updated. AGENTS now affirmatively selects aliases for tracker commands and reserves canonical UUIDs for identity-sensitive artifacts.

Scope/safety: additive output, no caller depends on alias absence, ambiguity remains fail-closed, no dependency added, no existing test weakened. make lint and make typecheck passed.

Siblings/parity: CLI summary and library summary both call summary_compute; MCP delegates to the library. No automated caller bypasses the shared core; dual-direction identity artifacts are the explicit canonical-ID negative control. No missing parallel surface.

Replication: repaired code produced 25/25 aliases under the full repository AGENTS context, 25/25 aliases with local field+rule, and 25/25 canonical rebar-ticket trailers. The original report no longer reproduces.

Landing: Gerrit change 1563 received LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1, had no unresolved comments, and was submitted/merged at 2026-08-09 18:46:53Z. No residual fragility observed beyond the fixed contract gap.

## Context

The compact ticket summary drops the resolved alias and echoes the caller-supplied identifier. In representative agent workflows, this makes four-character prefixes locally salient even though aliases are available elsewhere. The resolver correctly fails closed on ambiguous prefixes.

## Proven root cause

summary_compute resolves each ticket through show_state but omits state alias from its return payload. The summary schema, library/MCP docs, and compact report therefore institutionalize an alias-free shape. Agent guidance also lacks an adjacent affirmative selection rule: use aliases for tracker commands after discovery, while reserving canonical UUIDs for identity-sensitive artifacts.

A pinned behavioral evaluation discriminated the causes. Prefix-only local summaries produced 25/25 four-character commands. Adding aliases locally produced 25/25 alias commands. Adding the affirmative rule independently produced 25/25 aliases. Removing the quick-reference example or historical four-character references did not change identifier selection. The negative control produced 25/25 full UUID rebar-ticket trailers.

## Repair plan

- Add the exact resolved alias as an additive field on every resolvable summary result while preserving the current ticket_id echo contract and unknown/ambiguous fail-closed behavior.
- Update the summary JSON schema plus library, MCP, CLI, and reference documentation to expose the alias consistently.
- Add adjacent affirmative AGENTS guidance to use aliases in tracker commands after discovery and full canonical UUIDs in rebar-ticket trailers and other identity-sensitive artifacts.
- Add held-out regression coverage through the core/library, CLI JSON, and MCP/schema surfaces, including an ambiguous-prefix control.
- Re-run the pinned behavioral evaluation and its canonical-trailer negative control after the repair.

## Testing

- Run `pytest tests/unit/test_summary_alias_b68c.py tests/interfaces/contracts/test_schema_outputs.py` for the executable and schema contracts.
- Run `make lint` and `make typecheck` for repository gates.
- Run `python /tmp/rebar_alias_eval.py` with the pinned model/settings to measure the agent-selection and canonical-trailer controls.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Core and library summary results expose the exact resolved alias, checked by `pytest tests/unit/test_summary_alias_b68c.py`.
- [ ] CLI JSON summary output exposes the exact resolved alias, checked by `pytest tests/unit/test_summary_alias_b68c.py`.
- [ ] MCP summary output conforms to the alias-bearing schema, checked by `pytest tests/interfaces/contracts/test_schema_outputs.py`.
- [ ] Existing ticket_id echo semantics remain compatible, checked by `pytest tests/unit/test_summary_alias_b68c.py`.
- [ ] Ambiguous prefixes remain fail-closed, checked by `pytest tests/unit/test_summary_alias_b68c.py`.
- [ ] Agent guidance affirmatively prefers aliases for tracker commands, inspected in AGENTS.md.
- [ ] Agent guidance reserves canonical UUIDs for identity-sensitive artifacts, inspected in AGENTS.md.
- [ ] The held-out executable oracle is observed RED before the fix, GREEN after the fix, and RED again under alias-omission mutation.
- [ ] The pinned agent-selection evaluation produces at least 23/25 alias commands with zero four-character prefixes, checked by `python /tmp/rebar_alias_eval.py`.
- [ ] The negative control produces at least 23/25 full canonical UUID rebar-ticket trailers, checked by `python /tmp/rebar_alias_eval.py`.
